node.label: Community-engaged and Indigenous-led historical research
node.date_label: Roots: Yukon life histories 1974–90 · THOA by 1984 · Stó:lō field school 1998 · Smith 1999 · Wheeler 2005/2010 · TCPS 2 ch. 9 2010 · TRC 2015 · Shekon Neechie 2018 · CHA statement and open letter 2021 · reviewed through 2022
node.description: Historical research done with, by or under the direction of Indigenous communities, defined by how it is done. Winona Wheeler asks historians to treat Indigenous oral history 'as source and method': elders 'are not official documents; they are human beings and teachers', and 'one develops reciprocal relationships with them' (2010). Margaret Kovach locates method in relationship: 'it is not the method, per se' but its congruence 'with an Indigenous worldview' (2010). The Stó:lō field school's teachers wrote that historians 'could no longer in good conscience claim to be writing Aboriginal history when they were not speaking with Aboriginal people'; community staff set the questions and papers return to the Stó:lō archives (2009). Lianne Leddy, researching her own Serpent River First Nation, found university ethics review 'culturally inappropriate' (2010). Mary Jane Logan McCallum treats Indian Affairs archives as sites of possibility and contestation for Indigenous historians (2018). Shekon Neechie (2018) is 'entirely Indigenous conceived, created, and controlled'.

node.scope_note: A grouping created in revision 1.201 by splitting `indigenous`: it gathers practice defined by method (community direction, relationships, protocols, return of results), not by date or by the researcher's identity. Defined from practitioners' own statements, read in full: Wheeler 2010; Kovach 2010; Carlson, Lutz and Schaepe 2009; Leddy 2010; Macdougall 2010 (introduction) and 2018; McCallum 2018; Innes 2018; the Shekon Neechie launch (2018) and open letter (2021); McClellan and Gmelch (1992) on the Yukon collaboration; TCPS 2 chapter 9 (2022 text); SSHRC 2015 and current guidelines; the CHA statement (2021). Known through descriptions or named readers only: Kovach 2009, Shawn Wilson 2008, Innes 2013, McCallum 2014 (Williams 2016), Towards a New Ethnohistory 2018, Smith 2012/2021. Unread: Life Lived Like a Story itself, the Stó:lō–Coast Salish Historical Atlas, Auntie Rita, Native Historians Write Back, Indigenizing the Academy; OCAP's founding documents (year not sourced). Indigenous-authored critique stays in `indigenous`; settler scholarship about Indigenous peoples in `ethnohistory` and `native_newcomer`; works may belong to two. Collaboration does not erase different positions; community and university participants are credited separately. History PhD citation graph, release 2026-10-23: in Canadian History PhDs the community-engaged monographs are cited more than general methods texts (Macdougall 2010: 35 dissertations; McCallum 2014: 26; Life Lived: 25; Innes 2013: 13; Kovach 2009: 12; Shawn Wilson 2008: 11); context only. Reviewed through 2022: nothing read dates a 2023–24 development.

strands.title: Cree oral history as source and method
strands.focus: Wheeler writes as a Cree historian taught by Stan Cuthand, Ahenakew's protégé. She treats oral history 'as source and method': knowledge keepers establish their sources within their narratives, 'sort of like a "traditional footnote"', and the historian's task is 'to apply the teachings' as well as to study them (2010). Her 1998 critique of 'Indian–White relations' history sits on `native_newcomer`.
strands.works: Cree Intellectual Traditions in History (2010); The Othering of Indigenous History (1998)

strands.title: Relational research methodologies
strands.focus: Indigenous methodologists outside history define method as relationship. Shawn Wilson (Opaskwayak Cree): research is 'the ceremony of maintaining accountability to these relationships' (2008, publisher). Kovach: the conversational method is 'relational at its core'; a decolonizing perspective remains necessary but 'centres the settler discourse' and is 'not the epistemological centre' of an Indigenous methodology (2010). Smith's 1999 agenda is their shared reference. Macdougall (2018) notes that the method texts available to teachers are First Nations-specific.
strands.works: Decolonizing Methodologies (1999; 2012; 2021); Research Is Ceremony (2008); Indigenous Methodologies (2009); Conversational Method (2010)

strands.title: Kinship, community and the archive
strands.focus: Historians who read documentary records through their communities' concepts and relationships. Macdougall reconstructed community history from HBC, mission and scrip records and read them through wahkootowin, a Cree worldview of relatedness in her framing and a concept she credits to Métis Elder Maria Campbell, against a historiography 'preoccupied with race at the expense of culture' (2010). Innes points to Cowessess First Nation's own treaty-land research as the count of the 1880s starvation deaths that historians had not made (2018). McCallum describes reading Indian Affairs records about her own community and interpreting them with others (2018).
strands.works: One of the Family (2010); Elder Brother and the Law of the People (2013); 'Historians and Indigenous Genocide in Saskatchewan' (2018); 'Indigenous People, Archives and History' (2018)

strands.title: Research ethics and Indigenous governance of research
strands.focus: TCPS 2's chapter 9 (2010) opens by acknowledging that research 'has been defined and carried out primarily by non-Indigenous researchers'. It requires community engagement, including for 'interpretation of research results that will refer to Indigenous … history', exempts historical research on public records while asking for 'culturally informed advice', and cites OCAP from the First Nations Regional Longitudinal Health Survey (2022 text). SSHRC's 2015 guidelines make 'co-creation of knowledge' essential. The TRC (2015) asked SSHRC, archives and commemoration bodies to act (Calls 65, 70, 77–79). Leddy's 2010 critique shows how review looked from inside a community.
strands.works: TCPS 2, ch. 9 (2010); SSHRC guidelines (2015); TRC Calls to Action (2015); Leddy (2010)

strands.title: Indigenous historians' own institutions
strands.focus: Shekon Neechie (21 June 2018) describes itself as 'entirely Indigenous conceived, created, and controlled'; it counts community-trained and self-taught historians as historians and gives peer feedback from Indigenous historians. Its board (Macdougall, McCallum, Anderson, Corbiere, Hill, Wheeler, Innes) published an open letter supporting the CHA Council's 2021 genocide statement (13 August 2021).

proposed_edges.relationship: Community-directed and Indigenous-led practice reshapes oral history: relationships, protocols and community review, with interviews and papers returned to the community's own archive.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Rivera describes Aymara direction and return of results (existing rivera_oral reading); 'Each student's field school paper eventually finds its way to the Stó:lō archives, along with digital copies of any conducted interviews' (Carlson, Lutz and Schaepe 2009, p. 5); Leddy 2010 pp. 9–15 (storytelling as 'an important way for Indigenous peoples to be active participants and recognized experts in academic research', p. 9); Wheeler 2010 p. 48 ('reciprocal relationships'). Takes over the community-directed parts of edge_125, which stays on `indigenous` for Smith and Wilson.

proposed_edges.relationship: Historians of Native–newcomer relations could not 'in good conscience claim to be writing Aboriginal history when they were not speaking with Aboriginal people'; Métis history was 'preoccupied with race at the expense of culture'.
proposed_edges.map_label: Speak with the people written about
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Carlson, Lutz and Schaepe 2009, p. 4 (verbatim). Macdougall 2010, p. 14: 'Canadian scholars, like their American colleagues, have been overly preoccupied with race at the expense of culture.' Fairness: Macdougall calls Van Kirk and Brown's work 'pioneering' (p. 13), and the Stó:lō authors keep the name ethnohistory. Ends in Agent A's field; A to confirm.

proposed_edges.relationship: Indigenous-led method and Indigenous-authored critique share authors and aims but differ: one is defined by how research is done with communities, the other by Indigenous historical authority and critique.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Wheeler's 1998 critique (nnreq_stevenson_1998) and 2010 method chapter (pp. 47–59); Kovach 2010, p. 42 distinguishes a 'decolonizing perspective' from 'an Indigenous paradigm'; Shekon Neechie 2018 ('entirely Indigenous conceived, created, and controlled'). An editorial comparison between the two parts of the split, agreed with Agent B.

proposed_edges.relationship: Community archives and commemoration: field-school papers return to the Stó:lō archives, McCallum hopes for Indigenous roles in making and keeping records, and the TRC asked archives and commemoration to change.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Carlson, Lutz and Schaepe 2009, p. 5; McCallum 2018 (section on Library and Archives Canada, paraphrased: a hope for Indigenous roles in the making, storage and regulation of records); TRC Calls 70, 77, 78 and 79(ii) (Call 70 reassembled from a two-column PDF).

proposed_edges.relationship: Her agenda of self-determination in research is the shared reference of later Indigenous methodologists and historians; Kovach adds that a decolonizing lens 'is not the epistemological centre' of an Indigenous methodology.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Smith 1999, introduction pp. 1–5 (existing reading). Leddy 2010, p. 2 n. 6 quotes Smith p. 140 on 'indigenous criteria which can judge research "not useful", "not indigenous"' and n. 32 quotes p. 191 on 'the cultural ground rules of respect'; Kovach 2010, p. 42 cites Smith and qualifies the decolonizing lens; Macdougall 2018 lists Smith 1999 among the First Nations-specific method texts.

proposed_edges.relationship: Grandmother-to-granddaughter oral history 'rooted in a deep sense of kinship responsibility' and the authority of tribal and family historians become a model for historians researching their own communities.
